items.stem: What does the work-energy principle state?
options: work done equals the change in momentum
the work done by the resultant force equals the change in kinetic energy
items.answer: the work done by the resultant force equals the change in kinetic energy
items.markingKey: Equivalently, initial energy + work in = final energy + work out.

items.stem: Explain why a car descending a hill at constant speed must be doing work against resistance.
items.answer: Its KE is constant but it loses GPE; by the work-energy principle the lost GPE equals the work done against resistance (and braking).
items.markingKey: B1 KE constant, GPE lost; B1 equals work against resistance [2]

items.stem: A particle of mass 80 kg moves 40 m down a slope inclined at 20°, starting at 3 m s⁻¹, against a constant resistance of 60 N. Grace finds its final speed as 16.8 m s⁻¹. Explain the error and correct it.
items.answer: Grace has ignored the work done against the resistance (2400 J); (1/2)mv² = (1/2)mu² + 10,900 − 2400 gives v = 14.9 m s⁻¹.
items.markingKey: B1 resistance work omitted; B1 correct speed [2]

items.stem: A box of mass 5 kg is pulled from rest across a horizontal floor by a horizontal force of 20 N against a resistance of 10 N. Use the work-energy principle to find its speed after 10 m.

A 10 kg block sliding at 8 m s⁻¹ comes to rest after 10 m on a rough horizontal floor. Find the friction force, assumed constant.

items.stem: Explain how the work-energy principle is written for a particle moving down a slope against a resistance, and use it to find the final speed of a 10 kg particle starting at 5 m s⁻¹ and moving 5 m down a 15° slope against 20 N.
items.answer: Initial KE + loss of GPE − work against resistance = final KE: v = 5.56 m s⁻¹.
items.markingKey: B1 statement; B1 speed [2]

items.stem: A particle of mass 70 kg moves 5 m down a slope inclined at 10°, starting at 2 m s⁻¹, against a constant resistance of 20 N. Leila finds its final speed as 4.62 m s⁻¹. Explain the error and correct it.

items.markingKey: B1 resistance work omitted; B1 correct speed [2]

items.stem: Explain how the work-energy principle is written for a particle moving down a slope against a resistance, and use it to find the final speed of a 5 kg particle starting at 2 m s⁻¹ and moving 40 m down a 30° slope against 15 N.

items.stem: A particle moves 5 m along a slope inclined at 15°. Omar uses mg × 5 for the change in GPE. Explain the error.

items.stem: A car engine produces a driving force of 2000 N at 15 m s⁻¹. What is its power?
items.markingKey: P = Fv.

items.stem: Explain why a car working at constant power has a smaller driving force at higher speeds.
items.answer: P = Fv with P constant, so F = P/v decreases as v increases.
items.markingKey: B1 P = Fv; B1 F inversely proportional to v [2]

items.stem: A car of mass 1500 kg works at a constant 20 kW against a resistance of 1000 N. Lina says its acceleration is the same at all speeds. Explain why this is wrong.
items.answer: The driving force P/v decreases as v increases, so the resultant force (P/v − R) and hence a decrease: e.g. a = 0.444 m s⁻² at 12 m s⁻¹, and a = 0 at 20 m s⁻¹.
items.markingKey: B1 F = P/v decreases; B1 a decreases to zero at max speed [2]

items.stem: A car of mass 1000 kg has a maximum speed of 40 m s⁻¹ on a level road against a constant resistance of 1500 N. Find the power of the engine.

items.stem: Explain why a car working at a constant power of 50 kW against a constant resistance of 750 N has a maximum speed, and find it.
items.answer: As speed increases the driving force P/v falls until it equals the resistance; then a = 0. v_max = 50000/750 = 66.7 m s⁻¹.

items.stem: A particle of mass 80 kg moves 40 m down a slope inclined at 30°, starting at 5 m s⁻¹, against a constant resistance of 30 N. Grace finds its final speed as 20.6 m s⁻¹. Explain the error and correct it.
items.answer: Grace has ignored the work done against the resistance (1200 J); (1/2)mv² = (1/2)mu² + 16,000 − 1200 gives v = 19.9 m s⁻¹.
items.markingKey: B1 resistance work omitted; B1 correct speed [2]

items.stem: A particle moves 40 m along a slope inclined at 25°. Yusuf uses mg × 40 for the change in GPE. Explain the error.
items.answer: GPE depends on the vertical height: h = 40 sin 25° = 16.9 m, so ΔGPE = mgh.
items.markingKey: B1 vertical height needed; B1 h = d sin α [2]

items.stem: A car of mass 800 kg works at a constant 24 kW against a resistance of 500 N. Mei says its acceleration is the same at all speeds. Explain why this is wrong.
items.answer: The driving force P/v decreases as v increases, so the resultant force (P/v − R) and hence a decrease: e.g. a = 0.575 m s⁻² at 25 m s⁻¹, and a = 0 at 48 m s⁻¹.
items.markingKey: B1 F = P/v decreases; B1 a decreases to zero at max speed [2]

items.stem: A car of mass 1500 kg works at a constant 20 kW against a resistance of 800 N. Felix says its acceleration is the same at all speeds. Explain why this is wrong.
items.answer: The driving force P/v decreases as v increases, so the resultant force (P/v − R) and hence a decrease: e.g. a = 1.13 m s⁻² at 8 m s⁻¹, and a = 0 at 25 m s⁻¹.
items.markingKey: B1 F = P/v decreases; B1 a decreases to zero at max speed [2]

items.stem: A car of mass 1200 kg with power 50 kW climbs a hill (sin α = 1/25) against a resistance of 400 N. Aisha gives the maximum speed as 50000/400 = 125 m s⁻¹. Explain the error.
items.answer: Up the hill the driving force must also balance mg sin α = 480 N: v = 50000/(400 + 480) = 56.8 m s⁻¹.
items.markingKey: B1 weight component omitted; B1 correct speed [2]

items.stem: Explain why the same car (power 20 kW, resistance 800 N, mass 1000 kg) has a higher maximum speed down a hill with sin α = 1/40 than on the level, and find it.
items.answer: Down the hill the weight component helps: P/v = R − mg sin α, so v = 20000/(800 − 250) = 36.4 m s⁻¹.
